organism_context: Streptomyces sp. CL190 (mevalonate pathway); thiolase/KAS-III fold condensing enzyme, homodimer
rationale: KEGG EC 2.3.1.194 is acetoacetyl-CoA synthase (acetyl-CoA:malonyl-CoA C-acetyltransferase, decarboxylating), a single-activity KAS-III-fold condensing enzyme homologous to EC 2.3.1.180 but unable to use malonyl-ACP. The ModelSEED entry drops the acetoacetyl-CoA product entirely (snapshot status MI:C:-25/H:-35/N:-7/O:-18/P:-3/S:-1 = one acetoacetyl-CoA).
direction_note: The decarboxylative Claisen condensation is driven irreversibly by CO2 release, so acetyl-CoA + malonyl-CoA -> acetoacetyl-CoA + CoA + CO2 (the '>' sense) is the only direction the enzyme runs; ModelSEED's '<' would be CO2 fixation onto CoA.

organism_context: Methanocaldococcus jannaschii / methanogenic archaea; the best-characterised counterpart is the methylofuran polyglutamate ligase pair MyfA/MyfB (OrfY/Orf5) of Methylorubrum extorquens
rationale: MfnE/MfnF build only the methanofuran core APMF-Glu; the glutamate-chain extension that distinguishes methanofuran b/c/d is carried out by separate, still poorly assigned glutamate ligases (MyfB/Orf5 is the characterised analogue in methylofuran), so no single protein can be named for this six-glutamate lump. Equation writes six amide bonds as a bare dehydration with no ATP.
direction_note: Omitting the ATP that pays for six amide bonds makes the written condensation look uphill, which is exactly why ModelSEED defaults to the hydrolytic '<'; the biological flux is ligation toward methanofuran d.

enzyme_name: none identified - spontaneous hydrolysis of the ETH-NAD imine adduct
organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis ethionamide activation (downstream of the EthA Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenase and non-enzymatic radical addition to NAD)
rationale: Compound formulas confirm a plain imine hydrolysis (C29H34N9O14P2 + H2O + H+ -> NH3 + C29H33N8O15P2); the ETH-NAD adduct chemistry downstream of EthA is non-enzymatic, and no protein is assigned to this step. No enzyme could be identified, so functionality is left unknown rather than guessed.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of an imine to the ketone plus free ammonia is effectively irreversible at physiological ammonia levels, so the '>' sense is right; ModelSEED's '<' would require condensing NH3 back onto the adduct.

organism_context: Eubacterium limosum and other anaerobes; last step of the anaerobic DMB (cobamide lower ligand) pathway bzaABCDE
rationale: Hazra et al. established bzaABCDE as the complete anaerobic DMB pathway with 5-methoxy-6-methylbenzimidazole as the immediate precursor, leaving BzaE as the single radical-SAM catalyst of this last step; nothing indicates a second catalytic activity on the chain. The ModelSEED equation carries no cofactor at all and is one oxygen short (snapshot status MI:O:-1).
direction_note: The net methoxy-to-methyl conversion is a reductive, SAM-radical-driven step; with the reductant and SAM stripped out the written equation has no driving force, which is why ModelSEED reverses a biosynthetically one-way reaction.

rationale: Repeated literature searches on phosphonoformate (foscarnet) interconversion with phosphite and CO2 returned no enzyme: the hits are antiviral pharmacology, FosA inhibition and carbonic anhydrase binding, none of them a catalyst for this C-P/C-C chemistry. MetaCyc RXN-17526 sits in no pathway, so no catalysing protein can be named.
direction_note: Neither side has enzymological support - no enzyme is known to carboxylate phosphite (ModelSEED's '<'), and no phosphonoformate decarboxylase is described either, so the thermodynamic numbers are deciding an unanswered question.

enzyme_name: class A non-specific acid phosphatase (phosphotransferase mode), EC 3.1.3.2
organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa / enterobacterial NSAP family; used industrially to make L-ascorbate-2-phosphate
rationale: Bacterial class A acid phosphatases transfer the phosphoryl group from an activated donor (acetyl phosphate, pyrophosphate) to the ascorbate 2-OH via the same phospho-histidine intermediate used for hydrolysis - one catalytic activity, two acceptors, not a second active site. The ModelSEED entry omits the L-ascorbate-2-phosphate product altogether (status MI:C:-6/H:-6/O:-9/P:-1).
direction_note: Acetyl phosphate is the high-energy donor and acetate the leaving product, so phosphoryl transfer runs ascorbate -> ascorbate-2-phosphate ('>'); the reverse would have acetate attacking a phosphomonoester.

organism_context: Cicer arietinum (chickpea) and other legumes; GH1-family glucoside hydrolase of the maackiain/trifolirhizin interconversion cycle
rationale: The catalysing protein is only characterised at the level of chickpea isoflavonoid-conjugate beta-glucosidases rather than as a cloned trifolirhizin-specific enzyme, but all members of this class are single-active-site retaining glycoside hydrolases with no second catalytic function. Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry and the plant pathway, hence low confidence.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis to maackiain plus free D-glucose is irreversible in vivo; ModelSEED's '<' would need free D-glucose as a glucosyl donor, which no glucosyltransferase uses (the synthetic step goes through UDP-glucose).

enzyme_name: unknown (late tailoring step of the 8-O-methylfusarubin pathway)
organism_context: Fusarium fujikuroi / F. solani fsr (PKS3) polyketide cluster
rationale: Both species carry the identical formula C16H16O7 in the pinned snapshot, so this is an isomerisation (open hydroxy form to the cyclic hemiketal), not a redox step, and the late fsr-cluster tailoring steps have never been assigned to specific proteins - several are thought to proceed spontaneously. No catalysing enzyme could be named.
direction_note: MetaCyc places this step inside 8-O-methylfusarubin biosynthesis, so pathway flux runs toward the cyclic natural product ('>'), but if the step is a spontaneous hemiketal equilibrium the direction is set by the surrounding pathway rather than by any enzyme.

organism_context: Streptomyces griseochromogenes (blasticidin S) and S. arginensis (arginomycin)
rationale: Lee et al. (2025) showed cytosinine is produced by the PLP enzyme BlsH acting on the BlsE dehydration product, catalysing an alpha,beta-dehydration coupled to amination within one PLP active site - a single mechanistic cascade, not two separable catalytic activities. The ModelSEED entry's substrate/product pair is two H and two O apart (status MI:H:-2/O:-2), so the water/redox bookkeeping of this step is wrong and the MetaCyc intermediate predates the 2025 pathway revision.
direction_note: Flux runs toward cytosinine, the sugar core committed to blasticidin S by the downstream ATP-grasp ligase BlsI, so the '>' sense is the biosynthetic one.

organism_context: Plant cytosolic/plastidic DHARs (GST superfamily, single catalytic cysteine); in animals the same activity is carried by glutaredoxins and GSTO1 rather than a dedicated DHAR
rationale: DHAR is a GST-fold protein with one catalytic cysteine running a single thiol-transfer cycle; its GST-superfamily membership is ancestry, not a second catalytic activity. The ModelSEED entry drops the GSSG product (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2 = one glutathione disulfide).
direction_note: In the ascorbate-glutathione cycle the enzyme only reduces dehydroascorbate at the expense of GSH ('>'); with GSSG deleted from the equation the thermodynamic driving force disappears, which is what flips ModelSEED to '<'.

organism_context: Avena sativa (oat) primary leaves
rationale: Knogge and Weissenbock purified this OMT 180-fold from oat leaves and found a single methyl-transfer activity with a mono-iso Theorell-Chance mechanism and no transfer to pathway intermediates, i.e. one catalytic function. The ModelSEED entry omits the 7-O-methylvitexin-2''-rhamnoside product (status MI:C:-28/H:-31/O:-14).
direction_note: SAM-dependent O-methylation is effectively irreversible and the paper identifies it as the last step of the pathway, so '>' (SAM + acceptor -> SAH + methylated flavone) is the only physiological sense.

organism_context: Avena sativa (oat) mugineic-acid-family phytosiderophore biosynthesis
rationale: Formula arithmetic in the pinned snapshot confirms avenic acid A = 2'-deoxymugineic acid + H2O, i.e. hydrolytic opening of the azetidine ring, but the oat enzyme responsible has never been purified or cloned (searches return only root-exudate surveys). No protein can be named, so functionality stays unknown.
direction_note: DMA is the universal precursor of the mugineic-acid family, so biosynthetic flux is DMA -> avenic acid A ('>'); reclosing the azetidine ring with loss of water is not a known plant reaction.

organism_context: Thylakoid-lumen lipocalin of plants and algae; xanthophyll cycle
rationale: VDE is a single lipocalin-domain enzyme that performs only ascorbate-dependent epoxide opening; the opposite reaction belongs to a completely different protein, zeaxanthin epoxidase (ZEP, EC 1.14.15.21, NADPH + O2). The ModelSEED entry drops the two dehydroascorbate products (status MI:C:-12/H:-12/O:-12 = 2 x DHA).
direction_note: The xanthophyll cycle is two separate one-way enzymes, so ModelSEED's '<' hands ZEP's chemistry (and its O2/NADPH requirement) to VDE's equation; VDE itself only runs violaxanthin -> zeaxanthin.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous nitrite elimination with lactone formation
organism_context: Bradyrhizobium sp. strain JS329, 5-nitroanthranilic acid degradation; the step follows NaaB (5-nitrosalicylate 1,2-dioxygenase) and precedes the NaaC lactonase
rationale: Qu and Spain state explicitly that 'the nitro group is spontaneously eliminated as nitrite concomitant with the formation of a lactone from the ring fission product', so this entry has no enzyme behind it; functionality is unknown because there is no protein to classify, not because evidence is lacking.
direction_note: A spontaneous elimination that forms a lactone and expels nitrite does not run backwards, so the '>' sense is correct even though no enzyme sets it.

enzyme_name: acyl-glucose-dependent anthocyanin 5-O-glucosyltransferase (AA5GT), GH1 family - beta-glucosidase mode
organism_context: Delphinium grandiflorum and Dianthus caryophyllus (carnation) petals; a GH1 glycoside hydrolase recruited as a transglucosidase
rationale: The protein is a GH1 retaining glycosidase whose single catalytic pair performs both transglucosylation (acceptor = anthocyanin) and hydrolysis (acceptor = water) - one active site and one mechanism, so it does not meet the bar for bifunctional. Matsuba et al. characterised the acyl-glucose-dependent activity in these two genera.
direction_note: The physiological glucosyl donor is an acyl-glucose, never free D-glucose, so ModelSEED's '<' (glucose condensing onto cyanidin 3-O-glucoside) has no enzymatic route; only the hydrolytic '>' is chemically available as written.

organism_context: MetaCyc PWY-7057 cichoriin interconversion (Cichorium / coumarin-glucoside metabolism)
rationale: No literature could be found identifying the protein behind MetaCyc's 'cichoriin transglucosylase' - Europe PMC returns zero hits for cichoriin transglucosylation - so although the chemistry is a straightforward beta-glucoside hydrolysis, there is no named enzyme to classify and 'unknown' is the honest answer.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of cichoriin to esculetin plus free D-glucose is irreversible; the reverse as written would require free glucose to act as a glucosyl donor.

organism_context: Methanogenic archaea (Methanosarcina mazei, Methanothermobacter); membrane-bound eight-subunit MtrA-H complex with a corrinoid cofactor
rationale: Mtr is a multi-subunit membrane complex, not a fused multidomain chain: MtrH transfers the methyl group from CH3-H4MPT to the MtrA corrinoid and MtrA/MtrE methylate CoM while pumping Na+, so per the exclusion rule this is monofunctional. The ModelSEED entry omits the methyl-CoM product (status MI:C:-3/H:-8/O:-3/S:-2 = one methyl-coenzyme M).
direction_note: Mtr is a reversible Na+-translocating methyltransferase - it runs backwards in methylotrophic methanogenesis and in anaerobic methane oxidation - so the direction is really set by the Na+ gradient and pathway, but the canonical, dominant sense is CH3-H4MPT + CoM -> H4MPT + CH3-CoM ('>').

enzyme_name: delta-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase (P5CS / ALDH18A1); ProB + ProA in bacteria
organism_context: Plants, animals and fungi fuse both activities in one P5CS/ALDH18A1 polypeptide (Arabidopsis P5CS forms filaments that channel the intermediate); bacteria keep them as separate ProB and ProA proteins
rationale: MetaCyc's PROLINE-MULTI lumps the kinase and the NADPH-dependent reductase steps; in eukaryotes a single fused P5CS chain genuinely carries both catalytic activities, whereas E. coli ProB and ProA are separate (and recent work shows they do not even channel). The ModelSEED entry drops NADP+ (status MI:C:-21/H:-24/N:-7/O:-17/P:-3 = one NADP).
direction_note: With NADP+ deleted the written equation loses the redox leg that makes proline biosynthesis one-way; ATP hydrolysis plus NADPH oxidation drive glutamate -> glutamate-5-semialdehyde ('>'), and ModelSEED's '<' would amount to ATP synthesis from the semialdehyde.

organism_context: Bacterial single-domain rhodaneses (E. coli PspE, GlpE) and mammalian TSTD1/TST; human TST has two rhodanese domains but only one is catalytic
rationale: The catalyst is a rhodanese-fold sulfurtransferase running one ping-pong persulfide-transfer activity; a tandem rhodanese architecture is a duplicated fold with a single active cysteine, not a second catalytic activity. The ModelSEED entry omits the GSSG product (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2).
direction_note: The physiological role is thiosulfate reduction to sulfane sulfur / H2S at the expense of GSH ('>'); the ping-pong persulfide chemistry is intrinsically reversible, so the direction is really set by the thiol and persulfide pools, and the missing GSSG removes the term that would show it.

organism_context: Bacillus sp. NRRL B-21195 and Kribbella flavida; intracellular degradation of the cyclic tetrasaccharide produced from starch
rationale: The KEGG EC 3.2.1.204 entry gives a single configuration-retaining hydrolase that opens the cyclic tetrasaccharide and then cleaves the linear alpha-isomaltosyl-(1->3)-isomaltose - two successive turnovers of one catalytic activity, not two activities. Note the ModelSEED label 'Brachiose' for cpd00217 is isomaltose (abbreviation 'isomal').
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis of a strained cyclic tetrasaccharide to two isomaltose molecules is irreversible; ModelSEED's '<' would have the enzyme re-cyclise two free disaccharides with loss of water.

organism_context: Alcaligenes sp. strain BR60 (transposon Tn5271) and related 3-chlorobenzoate degraders; the step follows the two-component chlorobenzoate 3,4-dioxygenase CbaAB
rationale: CbaAB dioxygenates 3-chlorobenzoate at the 3,4 position to a gem-chlorohydrin cis-diol that collapses to protocatechuate with loss of HCl without a catalyst (protocatechuate accumulates directly on cba expression in E. coli); CbaC dehydrogenase handles the 4,5-diol branch instead. No enzyme runs this entry.
direction_note: Re-aromatisation with chloride release is strongly downhill and irreversible, so the '>' sense is right; chloride re-addition to protocatechuate is not a reaction.

enzyme_name: unknown (generic beta-D-glucosidase acting on the chromogenic substrate 4-methylumbelliferyl beta-D-glucoside)
organism_context: 4-MU-beta-D-glucoside is a laboratory assay substrate hydrolysed by many unrelated GH1/GH3 beta-glucosidases, so no single physiological enzyme belongs to this entry
rationale: This is an assay reaction rather than a metabolic step: the substrate is a fluorogenic reporter, and MetaCyc attaches it to no specific protein. Rather than stamp 'monofunctional' onto an unspecified glycosidase I record the enzyme as unidentified.
direction_note: Hydrolysis to 4-methylumbelliferone plus free D-glucose is irreversible; the '<' sense would need free glucose as a glucosyl donor.

organism_context: MetaCyc places this in PWY-7913 (firefly bioluminescence), where arbutin hydrolysis supplies the hydroquinone used for D-luciferin formation; arbutin-hydrolysing beta-glucosidases are widespread in bacteria and plants
rationale: The chemistry is a textbook retaining beta-glucosidase cleavage of arbutin to hydroquinone and D-glucose, a single catalytic activity, but the particular protein in the firefly pathway has not been identified, so confidence in the enzyme assignment is low.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is one-way; ModelSEED's '<' would require free D-glucose to glucosylate hydroquinone, which in vivo is done by a UDP-glucose glucosyltransferase instead.

organism_context: Bacterial ferritins and bacterioferritins; a 24-mer protein cage whose subunits each carry one di-iron ferroxidase centre
rationale: Ferritin is a homo-oligomeric cage, not a fused multidomain chain: every subunit runs the same ferroxidase activity and mineral nucleation is the physical consequence of it, not a second catalytic function. Confidently known enzymology, so no PMIDs were needed.
direction_note: O2-dependent Fe(II) oxidation and deposition as ferrihydrite is irreversible; ModelSEED's '<' would have the mineral spontaneously dissolve while regenerating O2, which is not a reaction any enzyme performs.

organism_context: Allium cepa / A. sativum, biosynthesis of the S-alk(en)yl-cysteine sulfoxide flavour precursors (PWY-5707, PWY-6176)
rationale: Yamaguchi and Kumagai describe this step only as conversion of the S-2-carboxypropyl conjugate 'by decarboxylation and oxidation', with no enzyme identified in either onion or garlic; product formulas in the snapshot are consistent with gamma-glutamyl-S-(1-propenyl)-L-cysteine. No protein can be named.
direction_note: The real step is an oxidative decarboxylation (CO2 plus a two-electron acceptor); MetaCyc balances the books by emitting 'formate' instead, which hides the oxidant that makes the biosynthetic '>' direction irreversible.
